_about: SEO Package 2 checkpoint. articles.<slug>.status is DONE (>= 1,600 words, verified batch) or REVIEW_REQUIRED (reason required); absent = PENDING. Written only after a batch passed its QA; the gate (scripts/seo-package2.js) re-measures every DONE article on each run. batches lists each published batch.

batches.notes: Group A, queue order of the second batch. Every article passed an independent verifier; pickup-or-delivery, Noi Bai arrival, first-time renting, best scooters and can-foreigners needed a fix round and passed a delta verification; automatic-vs-manual (one MAJOR, replaced with the verifier's wording) and the MINOR findings elsewhere were applied by the lead and checked by lint and QA. Recorded front matter changes: how-to-book title now carries its primary keyword ("Motorbike rental app Hanoi") and says there is no app; pickup-or-delivery description drops "and test-ride" (no test-ride policy in OWNER-FACTS); best-scooters description named three models, claimed what foreigners actually rent and lacked "Hanoi scooter rental"; can-foreigners description says deposit instead of cash deposit. Delivery-old-quarter title deliberately unchanged: a title with motorbike rental plus Hanoi Old Quarter would compete with the ranking /articles/renting-motorbike-old-quarter/. Removed or reworded original passages: how-to-book "both work for foreign numbers", "in Vietnamese or simple English" and three implied shop policies (photos on the spot, test ride and swap, booking secures the bike); how-to-rent "Shops will hand you a bike without asking" and the deposit-comes-back sentence; pickup-or-delivery test-riding lead clause, test-ride/swap, first ten minutes, deliverer present, deposit and contract travel, quickest deposit settlement, inside a few kilometres; Hoan Kiem one-way loop, actively enforced, roughly fifteen minutes and case-by-case delivery; Noi Bai 25-30 km (now 27 km from the Vietnam Airlines guide), the shop-cannot-hand-you-a-bike-at-the-terminal sentence and two unsourced airport-road claims; automatic-vs-manual The Vietnamese default, Learning time: minutes, less ground clearance, narrower/lighter/every roadside shop, cheapest and simplest (the day rates are equal); best-scooters three models dominate, most popular scooter in Vietnam, the unverified Click bodywork/running-gear sentence, suits most riders, the regular-unleaded/serviced-by-the-shop bullet; first-time automatics creep from idle (a centrifugal clutch is disengaged at idle), most visitors use, nerves wear off within a day; delivery-old-quarter ten minutes, about fifteen minutes' ride, identical to the shop version; can-foreigners the lead claim that foreigners rent every day with no residence status or bank account needed, stock changes week to week, return deposits, process takes minutes, foreigners rent here every day, the phone-number and residence-card lines, old A1 up to 175 cc, Under 50 cc, every fine amount (Decree 238/2026/ND-CP amends Decree 168/2024 from 15 August 2026 and its amended Article 18 could not be read). No weekly, monthly, 50cc or E-Bike price added (docs/seo/price-reconciliation.md). Legal correction outside the batch: motorbike-passenger-rules-vietnam and child-passengers-motorbike-vietnam said a child under 14 with an adult may be a second passenger; Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 33(1)(c), as quoted by the Government page both articles cite, says a child under 12 with no adult condition (re-read 2026-10-25). Findings for the owner: exploring-hoan-kiem-by-motorbike and hoan-kiem-walking-street-motorbike-visitors describe one continuous Friday-to-Sunday closure (the 2026 reports give 19:00-24:00 on each day) and omit Zone 1; renting-motorbike-old-quarter omits the Zone 1 evening restriction and keeps an unsourced fifteen-minute ride; do-hanoi-rentals-include-helmets, helmet-law-vietnam and renting-motorbike-hanoi-one-day state helmet policies not in OWNER-FACTS; motorbike-rental-requirements-hanoi and compulsory-motorbike-insurance-vietnam state insurance carried by the shop, against OWNER-FACTS; motorbike-rental-deposit-hanoi and returning-a-rental-motorbike-hanoi promise deposit return on the spot in cash; which-countries-idp-valid-vietnam and idp-validity-period-vietnam call an IDP without the national licence a document-carriage fine; the Decree 238/2026 amendment may affect fine amounts quoted across the legal guides; docs/MODEL-DATABASE.md gives the Vision as 110 cc where Honda publishes 109.5 cc and its Yamaha Sirius RC URL now returns 404.

batches.notes: Priority A rental money pages (long-term terms, return, inspection, problems, inclusions, audience pages), third batch. Every article passed an independent verifier; six-months, three-month, returning and expats-monthly passed on the first verification with MINOR findings; year, inspection checklist, common problems, what-is-included, English teachers and international students needed a fix round and passed a delta verification; the delta MINOR findings and the verifier MINOR findings elsewhere were applied by the lead with the verifier's wording and checked by lint and QA. Cross-article rule set by the lead: OWNER-FACTS does not say whether the registration certificate travels with a rental bike and the VERIFIED police-impound guide says it stays with the owner, so every batch-3 page writes it as a question (ask at handover which registration papers travel with the bike, the original or a certified copy). Recorded front matter changes: returning description no longer promises a ten-minute return and the deposit back in cash (OWNER-FACTS states neither); inspection-checklist description drops "thirty seconds" and now carries its primary keyword; common-problems description drops "the five problems that actually hit Hanoi renters" (unsourced) and names problems in order of when they happen; what-is-included description drops registration papers and "usually helmets" (neither in OWNER-FACTS) and states no insurance from Nguyen Tu. No title changed. Removed or reworded original passages: six-months the ~1,500 km sentence (kept as owner guidance, reworded) and the long-term habits list (support channel wording); three-month the negotiation heading sentence (folded into the terms table); returning ten minutes, nobody charges for dust, deposit back on the spot in cash, worth their two minutes, shops are reasonable about extensions, photos-fuel-handshake-cash (all unsourced or implied policy); year expect several visits (now "may include"), still wins for most expats (now "can suit"), the relationship paragraph (reworded); inspection-checklist thirty seconds, 2-3 cm chain play and fixed in minutes (unsourced), "number plates" (a motorbike carries one rear plate, Circular 79/2024), registration certificate with the bike and insurance certificate available (now questions), "no plates", sign-photograph-ride (photos come first); common-problems same five problems, keep the contract until the cash is back, stolen from sidewalks not guarded parking, pay for attended parking (absolute claims), registration certificate at the shop and take it with the bike (now a question); what-is-included honestly split, papers and third-party insurance ride with the bike, ask to see both, helmets at most shops (no helmet policy in OWNER-FACTS), third-party cover wording (now the owner's legal duty, within its limits and conditions), agreed fuel level (fuel conventions differ), the breakdown division sentence, the closing core-and-edges line; English teachers how most teachers start, typically two to four locations, automatic scooters dominate, maintenance included (now may include, as OWNER-FACTS words it); international students none removed (100% kept): corrective sentences follow the unsourced below-ownership-cost line, the keep-the-receipt line, the loose 50cc-class wording (moped definition from Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 34(1)(g)) and the Ninh Binh weekend line (support is primarily Hanoi and local). Link budgets: common-problems keeps 16 targets because it is an index of problems, each linked to the guide that covers it in full. Source reads after Firecrawl ran out of credits used Tavily extract (Law 36/2024/QH15 Articles 34, 56, 57 and 59; Circular 12/2025/TT-BCA Article 24). No weekly, monthly, 50cc or E-Bike price added (docs/seo/price-reconciliation.md).

batches.notes: Priority A choosing and riding pages (renting versus buying, scooter versus semi-automatic, parking, and the best-bike pages for commuting, tall riders, English teachers, day trips, Hanoi traffic, long distance and students), fourth batch. Every article passed an independent verifier; renting-vs-buying, scooter-vs-semi, where-to-park, commuting, tall riders, English teachers, day trips, Hanoi traffic, long distance and students each needed a fix round and passed a delta verification; the delta MINOR findings were applied by the lead with the verifier's wording and checked by lint and QA. Rules applied from writing-guide section 10: Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 56 (the rider carries the registration certificate itself, a certified copy only for a mortgaged vehicle with the bank's confirmation, the owner's compulsory insurance certificate, an electronic identification account under 56(3)); moped definition Article 34(1)(g) with age 16 under 59(1)(a); Circular 12/2025/TT-BCA Article 24(5)(a) for exchanged licences; Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT Article 6 for speed defaults (read 2026-10-25). Business limit: support is primarily for Hanoi and local use, so the day-trip and long-distance pages ask the shop before booking and imply no rescue, delivery, one-way rental or touring package. Recorded front matter changes: scooter-vs-semi description dropped "narrower, cheaper and fixable anywhere" (the widths and day rates refute it); where-to-park description dropped "typical fees" and "towing" (unsupported); tall-riders description dropped "longer seat and floor space" and "suits them best" (unsupported; the Air Blade 125 is shorter than the Vision); long-distance description dropped "rent the biggest bike your licence covers" and "full maintenance" (contradicted by the page and OWNER-FACTS) and now carries its primary keyword. No title changed. Removed or reworded original passages: renting-vs-buying purchase prices, used-bike prices and the 8-12 month break-even (unsourced, self-contradictory; replaced by a formula with no figures), the foreigner-registration and fine-band sentences (unsourced), insurance as the shop's problem (against OWNER-FACTS); scooter-vs-semi wider than an underbone, narrowest and lightest, lowest cost, thirty seconds (refuted by the widths and rates); where-to-park a few thousand dong per session, tolerated on most streets, red-and-white curbs, the riding-a-few-metres exception, towed or ticketed, most street lots close in the evening, prevents most losses (unsourced); commuting the serviceability bullet (now may include), commute standard and Ring Road (unsourced; the price figures in that sentence are kept verbatim), a hundred times a day; tall riders the low-180s height match; English teachers running costs trivial, any shop services them, exchange takes some weeks, one deposit for the term, parked all day, the break-even line, contract season; Hanoi traffic rarely clears 40 km/h, the licence-free 50 cc or e-bike item (now the moped definition); long distance highways flow at 50-80 km/h, every town can fix a Wave, fixable anywhere, the A1 sentence (now new A1 to 125 cc with the Article 89 transitional scope), agree in writing (now a question); students cheapest full motorbikes and roomier (the day rates are shared), fuel a rounding error, a few thousand dong parking, the fine costs more than a semester, the most opportunistic theft, students rent in waves; day trips none (100% kept). Price rule: existing sentences that carry a monthly figure (commuting) or the E-Bike day rate (students) keep those figures verbatim; no new weekly, monthly, 50cc or E-Bike figure was written (docs/seo/price-reconciliation.md). Source reads used Tavily extract (Firecrawl had no credits).

batches.notes: Priority A rental problem and audience pages (lost key, puncture, loose chain, outside repairs, high mileage, fuel policy, easiest and lightest bikes for beginners, digital nomads, female riders), fifth batch. Every article passed an independent verifier; lost-key passed after a fix round; punctured-tyre, easiest-beginners, lightest, loose-chain, outside-repair, high-mileage, fuel-policy and digital-nomads needed a fix round and passed a delta verification; female-riders passed on the first verification; the delta and verifier MINOR findings were applied with the verifiers' wording and checked by lint and QA. Rules applied: writing-guide section 10 (Law 36/2024/QH15 Articles 33, 34(1)(g), 56, 57, 59; Circular 12/2025/TT-BCA Article 24(5)(a)); OWNER-FACTS wording for maintenance (may include an oil change, chain adjustment and tension, tyre-pressure checks and normal inspection), consumables (may be the renter's responsibility), the ~1,500 km owner guidance and Hanoi/local support; no shop rule is implied for fuel, lost keys, outside repairs, helmets or records (all written as handover questions). Manufacturer figures only from docs/MODEL-DATABASE.md or Honda Vietnam owner's manuals read 2026-10-25 via TinyFish (Firecrawl had no credits). Recorded front matter changes and removed or reworded original passages: lost-key: description dropped "a replacement fee from your deposit, a wait while it is cut" (OWNER-FACTS publishes no lost-key charge or deposit deduction; now asks the shop what a replacement costs and how long it takes). Removed or reworded: a solvable problem with a known cost, many rental shops hold a spare, the replacement key cost paragraph, the cost settles against the deposit, agreed-charge item, the closing line (all unsourced or implied policy); Vision smart-key claim cut; Air Blade 160 smart key per docs/MODEL-DATABASE.md. punctured-tyre: description "typically the renter's consumable" became "may be the renter's consumable, so ask first" (OWNER-FACTS wording: may be the renter's responsibility depending on the situation). Removed or reworded: most common rental-bike event after refuelling, the road-debris rule stated as typical, tens of thousands of dong, paid in cash and not worth a negotiation, any tyre shop fixes it in minutes and they are everywhere (unsourced); the shop keeping condition records is a question; Yamaha publishes tyre type for two models, Honda sizes only. easiest-beginners: no front matter text change. Removed or reworded: top every list, low narrow seats and seat height kills it, small forgiving wheels, the roughly 100 kg class (now Honda's published 97 kg Vision and 96 kg Wave Alpha 110 figures), licence-free e-bike as the easiest machine (now Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 34 groups: pedal-assist bicycle and moped 50 cc / 4 kW / 50 km/h), thirty minutes in a parking lot, confidence on day two; Air Blade 160 needs class A on a new licence (Article 89 keeps older A1 below 175 cc). lightest: description dropped "Weight is what makes a new rider drop a bike" and "the lightest legal rental options" (unsourced cause; now names the published weights). Removed or reworded: nearly always the bike fell over, removes the single most common failure, both the light option and the legal one (no e-bike weight is published: "lightest class on the list" kept verbatim with its day rate under price-reconciliation rule 2 and qualified as a general description), the light mainstream motorbikes sentence (the daily figures are reworded into the table), the Latte 125 and kerb-weight-table pointer, availability moves fastest; unverified Sirius FI 98 kg and Wave Alpha versions cut. loose-chain: description dropped "a five-minute adjustment at the shop" (unsourced). Removed or reworded: the most common mechanical complaint, 2-3 cm of play (now the Honda Vietnam owner's manual figures: Wave Alpha 25-35 mm and manual 32K57A100 for models AFS110MS/MD/MCS 30-40 mm, do not ride beyond 50 mm, read 2026-10-25), five minutes, explicitly the owner's maintenance (now OWNER-FACTS: maintenance may include chain adjustment and tension), the third-party sentence (now points to the outside-repair rules), any roadside mechanic for a small cash fee. outside-repair: no front matter text change. Removed or reworded: nine times out of ten, the shop's advice is free, puzzles are decided against the renter by default, the long-distance pointer, report at return (now the same day as well as at return); maintenance wording now "may all be part of that"; the yes-list heading now says confirm by phone first. high-mileage: no front matter text change. Removed or reworded: owner guidance from experience (now OWNER-FACTS: periodic checks around every ~1,500 km of use, not a manufacturer interval), a bike that changes hands every few weeks (now a rental bike), the shop's maintenance list with brake pads and cables (now the OWNER-FACTS may-include list), the 110-125 cc wear prediction (now: what has worn depends on the bike, the load, the roads and the rider), maintenance is the shop's side of the deal (now may be), the commute article's monthly-rate arithmetic (that article has none; now the commuter's side of a monthly rental), no charge for the shop's own maintenance items (not in OWNER-FACTS; now confirm which apply). fuel-policy: description dropped "usually near-empty" and "Petrol is cheap and stations are everywhere" (unsourced market norm implying a shop rule; OWNER-FACTS states no fuel rule). Removed or reworded: fuel is always the renter's (twice), most Hanoi rentals hand over a small noted amount (now one convention you may be offered), petrol costs and the fill-from-empty figure (unsourced), the far-provinces line, RON 92 as the standard grade and not fussy (now the Honda Wave Alpha owner's manual: RON 91 or higher for the Vietnam type, ethanol 10% or less, fill to the lower edge of the filler neck, read 2026-10-25), no shop refunds the petrol left (implied policy; now a question); the range figures are stated calculations from published tank and consumption figures. female-riders: no front matter text change. Removed or reworded: thousands of women, one of the most gender-equal motorbike cities, slow average speeds (unsourced statistics and ranking), confidence machines for all riders (now the class the beginner guide puts first), helmet included with most rentals (not in OWNER-FACTS; now a handover question; the helmet duty is Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 33), only while parked (ambiguous; now the compartment while riding), the one-minute demo (invented duration), the realistic-picture close (unsourced claims about attendants and shops); bag-snatching is now quoted from the UK FCDO Vietnam travel advice (read 2026-10-25), its on-foot advice marked as such. digital-nomads: no front matter text change. Removed or reworded: better than any other transport (unsupported superlative), maintenance included on Nguyen Tu rentals (now OWNER-FACTS: may include; consumables may be the renter's), under-seat compartments hold a backpack (now a handover check), attended lots at coworking spaces and malls (unsourced), a Saturday away and the best part of the weekend (support is primarily for Hanoi and local use, so trips are agreed with the shop first); the existing Click/Mio and Vision monthly figures are kept verbatim (price-reconciliation rule 2, DIFFERENT cell, owner review). No title changed. Price rule: no new weekly, monthly, 50cc or E-Bike figure; existing sentences with such figures (lightest E-Bike day rate, digital-nomads monthly figures) are kept verbatim (docs/seo/price-reconciliation.md rule 2).
